speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: asked the Minister for Manpower for companies implementing the Progressive Wage Model (PWM) and effecting the higher wage rungs, what assistance and interventions from the Ministry are available for such companies facing difficulties renegotiating ongoing multi-year contracts that have been signed before the PWM wage rungs are set.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This is why the tripartite cluster committees negotiate a multi-year schedule of wage increases for each PWM sector, to provide both service buyers and service providers with clarity on how progressive wages will increase in the years ahead.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The wage schedules are also announced in advance, so that service providers and buyers entering into new contracts do so with sufficient information, and those midway through existing contracts can discuss whether the contracts need to be re-negotiated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Tripartite Partners encourage service buyers to work closely with service providers to re-negotiate ongoing contracts where reasonable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The Government is also doing its part to offset increases in labour costs through the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme (PWCS).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This includes wage increments given due to Progressive Wage requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Beyond this, service buyers should consider moving towards outcome-based contracting.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This will encourage service providers to invest in productivity solutions and deploy manpower more efficiently, which is a win-win outcome as it supports sustainable wage growth and can also lead to better services to service buyers.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Business owners who are service sellers in multi-year contracts have given me feedback that they may be locked into contracts which may be up to 10 years, especially if this is related with longer-term municipal and infrastructure maintenance projects.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This may go beyond the length of Government support, like the PWCS which is five years.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: What recourse would businesses have should they be faced with such challenges?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Would the Ministry investigate such claims and educate service buyers, especially in the PWM rollout process as uplifting our lower wage workers is a whole-of-community effort?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: There are some exceptions, as the Member has mentioned, but these are typically in the minority with some peculiarity, such as waste management, for example, which runs up to seven years.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But that is one feature of our PWM's negotiations, in the sense that the Tripartite Partners are all involved – you have got the unions, the industry, service buyers, and even the Government being a service buyer too, are involved in the negotiation of the wage ladders.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Therefore, there is that realism that is injected where we, the Tripartite Partners in the cluster committees, understand what the practices are, what the typical renewal cycles are and how the contracts are structured to make sure that this is sustainable.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Therefore, it is expected that as we implement wage ladders, these have to be realistic in terms of the multi-year schedules.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In this case, with the recent increase, I acknowledge that we are in a phase where there are stronger growth prospects that we expect or we want for our low-wage workers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But these are how we manage and try to support the industry, to make sure that it does not overburden the industry.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: More importantly, over the long term, we hope that this remains sustainable.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I hope that the Member takes this into account and the unions can also do their part to help to mediate between the service buyers and contractors, for the benefit of their workers too.
